S030.note: Disagreement resolved by the map author to exclusion: the comparison of online with offline gamblers appears in the introduction only; the review's own synthesis reports prevalence of problematic online gambling and its correlates (sex, school grades), the same as a prevalence study of problematic use with no condition analysis.

S056.note: Disagreement resolved by the map author to inclusion: the review synthesizes how chatbots, including general-purpose LLMs used by people in acute distress, respond to suicide, self-harm and crisis risk, a finding on how the exposure meets the condition. Full text not accessible.

S082.note: Disagreement resolved by the map author to inclusion: the under-identification of suicide risk comes from evaluations of general-purpose ChatGPT, not from ChatGPT tested as a treatment, and lay use in the wild is part of the synthesis.

S085.note: Disagreement resolved by the map author to inclusion: the review synthesizes higher emotional distress among scam victims, and psychological distress is a symptom-level measure under R1.

S161.note: Disagreement resolved by the map author to inclusion: the review compares adolescents with neurodevelopmental conditions and typically developing peers on how they respond to cyberbullying, a finding on the exposure.

S185.note: Disagreement resolved by the map author to inclusion: the results name chatting on the internet as the second most endangering circumstance, and girls with intellectual disabilities were more likely than controls to chat with people online.

S250.note: Disagreement resolved by the map author to exclusion (E4): the chatbots reviewed are purpose-built clinical interventions, coded the same way as the dementia, rehabilitation and cognitive disability chatbot reviews (S191, S192, S202).

S251.note: Disagreement resolved by the map author to inclusion: misinformation prevalence is synthesized by condition topic (higher for neurodivergence content), coded the same way as the epilepsy content review (S255).
